title: Nourishing Fermented Korean Cornmeal Mandu JJigae
description: A sour, molten, solo-dinner Korean dish featuring white cornmeal, long-fermentation-dough, and Buddhist-temple-friendly ingredients, served in a solo mandu form and a donabe vessel.
instructions: Combine Korean cornmeal and water in a large bowl, mix until smooth.
Add rice flour, fermented Korean chili flakes, gochujang, sesame oil, garlic, Korean pear, soy sauce, black pepper, and mix until dough forms.
Knead dough for 10 minutes until it becomes smooth and elastic.
Wrap dough in plastic wrap and let it ferment at room temperature for 24-48 hours.
Divide dough into 4-6 equal pieces and roll each piece into a ball.
Flatten each ball into a thin circle, about 1/8 inch thick.
Place a small amount of fermented Korean greens in the center of each circle, fold the dough over, and press edges together to seal the mandu.
Heat donabe over medium heat until it reaches 180°F.
Cook mandu for 5-7 minutes on each side, until it is golden brown and crispy.
Serve hot, garnished with scallions and additional fermented Korean greens if desired.
Let the dish sit for 5 minutes before serving to allow flavors to meld together.
Use a slotted spoon to remove mandu from donabe and place on a plate.
